summary.name: File manager
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing file managers (file browsers): what they do, their history, and the main families such as orthodox, navigational, spatial, 3D and web-based file managers.
use_cases: learning the history of file managers
finding dual-pane or commander-style file managers
researching file picker and file transfer features
summary.what_it_does: The page is a general encyclopedia article about file managers, which are programs providing a user interface to create, open, rename, copy, move, delete, search and set permissions on files and folders. It describes common features such as copy/paste and drag-and-drop, transfer progress display, conflict handling (rename, overwrite or skip), and network access via FTP, SMB, NFS or WebDAV. It then surveys categories: orthodox (Norton Commander-style, two-panel) managers, navigational tree-based managers such as Windows Explorer and Nautilus, spatial managers, 3D managers, and web-based managers written in server-side languages. It also covers the history of directory editors and early file-list managers.
notable: Covers orthodox two-panel managers such as Norton Commander and its many descendants
Traces history from early directory editors like DIRED and flist
Describes spatial and 3D file manager concepts with examples
caveats: The article notes it needs more citations
3D file browsing has not become popular and lacks common standards
